title: Towards Ultra Scalability of Non-Volatile Magnetic Tunnel Junctions with a 3D Storage Layer
authors: Nuno Caçoilo, Shunsuke Fukami, Olivier Fruchart, Ioan-Lucian Prejbeanu
abstract: The perpendicular Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory is one of the most promising emerging non-volatile memory technologies, based on ultra-thin magnetic tunnel junctions. However, as these devices are limited by their thermal stability factor at technological nodes smaller than 20 nm, their scalability is compromised. A possible solution to this limitation relies on taking advantage of the shape anisotropy, by increasing substantially the thickness of the storage layer. Thanks to the combination of a vertical aspect-ratio and enhanced volume, high thermal stability can be maintained at sub-10 nm nodes. Here, we present the technological advancements and understanding of the magnetisation reversal that led to faster switching speeds at reduced switching voltage, providing a viable approach for dense arrays of ultra-small magnetic tunnel junctions.
summary: This paper tackles the critical scalability issue in pSTT-MRAM by proposing the use of 3D storage layers to enhance shape anisotropy. By understanding the physics of magnetization reversal, the authors demonstrate a viable path to maintain high thermal stability and achieve faster switching speeds in ultra-small magnetic tunnel junctions.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the scalability of Perpendicular Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory (pSTT-MRAM) devices, which suffer from insufficient thermal stability at nodes smaller than 20 nm.
main_result: The authors propose that maintaining high thermal stability at sub-10 nm nodes is viable by leveraging shape anisotropy through the use of a 3D storage layer structure.
method: The work combines technological advancements with theoretical understanding of magnetization reversal dynamics to achieve faster switching speeds at lower voltages.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Magnetic Tunnel Junction (MTJ), which utilizes ultra-thin magnetic tunnel junctions incorporating a fixed reference layer and a free storage layer.
key_observables: Thermal stability factor ($\Delta$), Tunnel Magnetoresistance (TMR), switching speed, and switching voltage.
important_parameters: Device node size (sub-10 nm), shape anisotropy, and the required TMR ratio ($\ge 200\%$).
main_assumptions: The approach relies on enhancing the volume and vertical aspect-ratio of the storage layer to counteract the loss of thermal stability as dimensions shrink.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the memory hierarchy (speed vs. density), and Figure 2 provides schematics of different MRAM designs showing the reference and storage layers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the scalability limits of pSTT-MRAM, then proposing the 3D storage layer solution, and finally detailing the technological advancements and physics governing magnetization reversal for ultra-small junctions.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the underlying physics of magnetization dynamics, energy barriers, and stability in nanoscale magnetic systems touches upon concepts relevant to engineered quantum states and energy landscapes in open quantum systems.
